records.title: API Reference
records.description: Every public endpoint, generated from the OpenAPI spec, plus the risk scale, flag codes and errors.
records.content:
## Base URL

| Environment | Base URL |
|---|---|
| Production | `https://api.provd.tech/v1` (placeholder during early access) |
| Local | `http://localhost:8000/v1` |

All requests and responses are JSON. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.

## Authentication

Endpoints marked **API key** take your key in the `X-API-Key` header. Public endpoints need no key and are rate-limited per IP.

```bash
curl -s https://api.provd.tech/v1/actions/evaluate \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PROVD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"chain":"tron","intent_type":"p2p_trade","counterparty":{"wallet_address":"T…"},"rails":{"fiat_rail":"mpesa","crypto_asset":"USDT_TRC20"},"amounts":{"fiat":65000,"fiat_currency":"KES","crypto":500}}'
```

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on evaluate: retries with the same key return the original decision and are not charged again.

## Errors

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` / `403` | Missing, invalid or inactive API key. |
| `402` | Free quota (or monthly plan) used and no balance. The body has `balance`, `units_required`, `purchase_url` and `topup_endpoint`. See [pay as you go](/docs/pay-as-you-go). |
| `404` | Decision or `intent_id` not found for your account. |
| `422` | Invalid body, invalid address, unsupported chain on the public check, or a reused `intent_id`. Body: `{"detail": "…"}`. |
| `429` | Too many requests. Wait a minute and retry. |
| `5xx` | Our side, or the chain data provider. Safe to retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`. |

Scored today: `p2p_trade`, `ramp_conversion`, `payout` and `otc_settlement` on `tron`. Chains and intent types we know but don't score yet (`stellar`, `solana`, `evm`; `swap`, `deposit`, `payment`…) are accepted and return `recommended_action: "not_yet_supported"` with a `NOT_YET_SUPPORTED` flag. They are not charged.

## Optional inputs that sharpen a score

| Field | Used by | What to send |
|---|---|---|
| `amounts.crypto` or `amounts.fiat` + `fiat_currency` | `amount_pattern` | The amount. Provd learns your own baselines from it: per counterparty, and your 90-day p99 per intent type. |
| `float_available` | `float_and_timing` | Your available float on this rail, in `amounts.fiat_currency` (payouts, OTC). |
| `account_signals` | `account_takeover_proxies` | Timestamps from your SIM-swap, device-trust or KYC provider: `sim_swap_at`, `device_changed_at`, `credentials_changed_at`, `payout_destination_added_at`, `account_created_at`, plus `provider`. Provd doesn't detect these itself; send what you have. |

Signals with nothing to work on report `none` in `signal_coverage` and add no risk.

## Risk scale

| Score | `risk_level` | `recommended_action` |
|---|---|---|
| 0–249 | `low` | `release` |
| 250–499 | `medium` | `manual_review` |
| 500–749 | `high` | `hold` |
| 750–1000 | `critical` | `reject` |

## Flag codes

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CP_ADDRESS_FROZEN` | critical | The counterparty wallet is itself on a public risk list (for example, frozen by Tether). |
| `CP_FLAGGED_EXPOSURE` | high | The wallet transacted directly with wallets on a public risk list. |
| `CP_INCIDENTAL_EXPOSURE` | medium | Exposure to listed wallets is a small share of volume across many counterparties, as with exchanges. |
| `CP_PLATFORM_FLAGGED_EXPOSURE` | high | The wallet transacted with wallets you confirmed as fraudulent. |
| `CP_NEW_WALLET` | low | First USDT activity in the last 7 days, with few transfers. |
| `CP_NO_HISTORY` | low | No USDT transfers found for this wallet. |
| `OWN_FRAUD_HISTORY` | critical | You reported confirmed fraud or a fake payment confirmation from this counterparty in the last 180 days. |
| `OWN_REVERSAL_HISTORY` | medium or high | You reported reversals, refunds or chargebacks from this counterparty in the last 180 days. |
| `VELOCITY_SPIKE` | medium | Unusually many checks for this counterparty in the last 24 hours. |
| `AMOUNT_SPIKE` | medium or high | Much larger (5x+, 20x+ for high) than this counterparty's largest previous amount with you. |
| `AMOUNT_ABOVE_PLATFORM_P99` | medium | Larger than 99% of your amounts for this intent type over 90 days (needs 30+ decisions). |
| `AMOUNT_STRUCTURING` | high | Three or more amounts just under a reporting threshold for this counterparty in 24 hours. |
| `RAPID_PASS_THROUGH` | high | Funds covering this amount arrived in the wallet within the last hour. |
| `FLOAT_STRAIN` | medium | The amount uses more than half of your available float. |
| `OFF_HOURS` | low | Fewer than 2% of your checks happen at this UTC hour. |
| `SIM_SWAP_RECENT` | high or critical | SIM swap in the last 72 hours; critical within 24 hours together with a new payout destination. |
| `DEVICE_CHANGE_WITH_ACCOUNT_CHANGE` | high | New device in the last 24 hours plus a new payout destination or credential change. |
| `NEW_PAYOUT_DESTINATION` | low | Payout destination added in the last 72 hours. |
| `NEW_ACCOUNT` | medium | Account opened in the last 24 hours. |
| `TOKEN_HONEYPOT`, `TOKEN_BLACKLIST_FUNCTION`, `TOKEN_MINTABLE`, `TOKEN_PAUSABLE` | varies | Risky token contract properties (`ramp_conversion` only). |
| `REDUCED_SIGNAL_COVERAGE` | info | A data source was unavailable, so a signal ran on partial data. |
| `NOT_YET_SUPPORTED` | info | The chain or intent type isn't scored yet. |

## Decision records

`GET /v1/decisions/{intent_id}` returns the signed record behind a score, with its Merkle proof and Bitcoin anchor once sealed. `merkle` and `batch` are `null` until the record joins a batch (within minutes). See [decision records](/docs/decisions), or paste a record into [Verify a decision](/verify).

records.title: Changelog
records.content:
## 2026-10-03

- Provd now scores money movement on African rails before funds are released. First coverage: USDT on Tron, with M-Pesa and bank rails as fiat context.
- New API under `/v1`: `POST /v1/actions/evaluate`, `GET /v1/decisions/{intent_id}`, `POST /v1/outcomes`, `GET /v1/counterparties/tron/{address}`, `GET /v1/usage`, `GET /v1/pricing`, `POST /v1/topups`, `GET /v1/topups`.
- Pay as you go: 100 free checks a day, then prepaid bundles topped up with USDT (TRC-20) or M-Pesa.
- Public [counterparty check](/check) on the website.
- Earlier APIs under `/api/v1` and their documentation have been retired.

records.title: Decision records
records.description: What Provd records for every check, and how to verify a record hasn't changed.
records.content:
Every call to `POST /v1/actions/evaluate` writes a decision record: what you asked, which signals ran, what they found and what Provd recommended. The response carries the record's hash as `decision_record_hash`, so you can store it next to the trade in your own system.

When a dispute, an auditor or a regulator asks why a release went ahead, you can show the record and prove it is the one produced at the time.

## What's in a record

| Field | Contents |
|---|---|
| `intent_id` | Your reference for the trade. |
| `intent` | The intent as you sent it: chain, intent type, counterparty (wallet address, phone hash), rails, amounts, context. |
| `signals` | Each signal that ran, its value, its contribution to the score, the reason and source references. |
| `signal_coverage` | For each signal, whether it ran on `full`, `partial` or `none` of its data. |
| `decision` | Score, risk level, recommended action and flags. |
| `engine_version` | The scoring engine version that made the decision. |
| `created_at` | When the decision was made (UTC). |

Records hold hashed phone identifiers only, never raw numbers.

## Fetch a record

```bash
curl -s https://api.provd.tech/v1/decisions/order-48213 \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PROVD_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "intent_id": "order-48213",
  "record": { "intent_id": "order-48213", "intent": { "…": "…" }, "signals": [], "signal_coverage": {}, "decision": {}, "engine_version": "2026.10.0", "created_at": "2026-10-03T13:11:16.891600+00:00" },
  "record_hash": "7eb6c86d3878be10e32acfe84a9ce9f0d923c75f67be6e839b173112c91164a5",
  "hash_algorithm": "sha256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace)",
  "signature": { "algorithm": "ecdsa-secp256k1-sha256", "key_id": "f0f85b25dd51b813", "public_key": "02…", "value": "…128 hex…" },
  "merkle": { "leaf_index": 0, "proof": [{ "side": "right", "hash": "…" }], "root": "26c31c7e…", "algorithm": "…" },
  "batch": { "batch_id": "e0a03a1e-…", "merkle_root": "26c31c7e…", "leaf_count": 2, "sealed_at": "…",
             "anchor": { "method": "opentimestamps", "status": "anchored", "reference": "bitcoin:block:…", "proof_url": "/v1/proof/batches/e0a03a1e-…/ots" } },
  "proof_status": "anchored"
}
```

You can only fetch decisions made with your own keys.

## How the proof works

1. **Hash.** The record is serialized as canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8) and hashed with SHA-256. That is `decision_record_hash`, returned the moment you call evaluate.
2. **Signature.** Provd signs the hash with a dedicated secp256k1 key (compact `r‖s`, low-S). The public key is published at `GET /v1/proof/keys`; pin it in your system.
3. **Batch.** Every few minutes, new decisions are sealed into a Merkle tree (`leaf = SHA256(0x00‖hash)`, `node = SHA256(0x01‖left‖right)`, odd node promoted). Your record gets an inclusion proof against the batch root.
4. **Anchor.** The batch root is timestamped on **Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps**. The proof is `pending` straight away and becomes `anchored` once the calendar's Bitcoin transaction confirms, usually within a few hours. Nobody — including Provd — can later change a record without breaking this chain.

`proof_status` tells you where a record is: `signed — joins the next batch within minutes` → `anchoring` → `anchored`.

## Verify a record yourself

The quickest way is in the browser: paste the JSON into [Verify a decision](/verify). It recomputes the hash, checks the signature and folds the Merkle proof on your device; nothing is sent to Provd.

For scripts and CI, download the verifier ([verify_decision.py](/tools/verify_decision.py)) and run it on a saved decision:

```bash
curl -s https://api.provd.tech/v1/decisions/order-48213 -H "X-API-Key: $PROVD_API_KEY" > decision.json
pip install cryptography
python verify_decision.py decision.json --public-key <public_key from /v1/proof/keys>
```

```
[ok] record hash 7eb6c86d…
[ok] signature by key f0f85b25dd51b813
[ok] merkle inclusion, leaf 0 -> root 26c31c7e…
[..] anchor: opentimestamps anchored bitcoin:block:…
```

It exits non-zero if anything fails — change one field in the record and the hash and signature checks fail.

To check the anchor independently, download the batch proof and use the official OpenTimestamps client:

```bash
curl -s -o batch.ots https://api.provd.tech/v1/proof/batches/<batch_id>/ots
pip install opentimestamps-client
ots verify -d <merkle root> batch.ots
```

### Just the hash, in a few lines

```python
import hashlib, json
canonical = json.dumps(resp["record"], sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
assert hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == resp["record_hash"]
```

Use a JSON serializer that keeps numbers exactly as received. Some languages rewrite numbers such as `1.0` as `1`, which changes the hash.

records.title: Pay as you go
records.description: Free daily checks, prepaid bundles and top-ups with USDT or M-Pesa. No monthly plan.
records.content:
Provd is prepaid, like airtime. You use free checks first, then checks you've bought. There is no subscription and no minimum term. (Global payout platforms can ask for a monthly plan instead; see the end of this page.)

## 1. Free quota

Every account gets **100 free checks a day**, reset at 00:00 UTC. Free checks are used before your balance.

A scored `POST /v1/actions/evaluate` uses one check. These don't use any:

- Requests that return `recommended_action: "not_yet_supported"` (for example `chain: "stellar"` or `intent_type: "swap"`).
- Retries with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
- `GET /v1/decisions/...`, `POST /v1/outcomes`, `GET /v1/usage` and the public counterparty check.

Check where you stand at any time:

```bash
curl -s https://api.provd.tech/v1/usage -H "X-API-Key: $PROVD_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "free_daily_checks": 100,
  "free_used_today": 37,
  "free_remaining_today": 63,
  "balance_checks": 9800,
  "paid_checks_30d": 200,
  "paid_units_30d": 200
}
```

## 2. When you run out: 402

When the free quota is used up and your balance is empty, evaluate returns `402 Payment Required` instead of a score:

```json
{
  "detail": "Free daily checks used and no prepaid balance. Buy a bundle to continue.",
  "balance": 0,
  "units_required": 1,
  "purchase_url": "https://provd.tech/pricing",
  "topup_endpoint": "/v1/topups"
}
```

Decide in your own code what a 402 means for the trade. Most platforms fall back to their manual review queue so nothing is released unchecked.

## 3. Bundles

Early-access pricing (the live list is at `GET /v1/pricing`):

| Bundle | Checks | Price | Per check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `10k` | 10,000 | $150 | $0.015 |
| `100k` | 100,000 | $1,000 | $0.010 |
| `1m` | 1,000,000 | $7,000 | $0.007 |

## 4. Top up

Start a top-up with the bundle and how you'll pay:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.provd.tech/v1/topups \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PROVD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "bundle": "10k", "method": "usdt_tron" }'
```

The response tells you exactly what to pay and where:

- **`usdt_tron`**: send exactly `amount_due` USDT (TRC-20) to `pay_to`. The exact amount identifies your payment.
- **`mpesa`**: pay `amount_due` KES to the paybill in `pay_to`, using the account number in `instructions`.

The top-up stays `pending` until the payment is confirmed, then your balance is credited. List your top-ups with `GET /v1/topups`.

Auto top-up (refill when your balance drops below a threshold) is coming.

## Monthly plans for global platforms

Payout platforms with steady volume can have a monthly plan instead: a set number of included checks per billing month, and a choice of what happens after they're used — draw from a prepaid balance, invoice the overage, or stop with `402`. `GET /v1/usage` then returns `billing_model: "subscription"` and a `plan` block with checks used and remaining this period. Plans are set up by us; [contact us](mailto:hello@provd.tech?subject=Provd%20monthly%20plan).

records.title: Score your first P2P trade in 10 minutes
records.description: Send a USDT-on-Tron trade to Provd before you release it, read the decision, and report what happened.
records.content:
## What you need

- An API key. Email [hello@provd.tech](mailto:hello@provd.tech) and we'll send one. Every key includes 100 free checks a day.
- The counterparty's Tron wallet address for a trade you're about to settle.

Base URLs:

```
https://api.provd.tech/v1     # production (placeholder during early access)
http://localhost:8000/v1      # local development
```

All requests and responses are JSON. Send your key in the `X-API-Key` header.

## 1. Check the counterparty (no key needed)

Before wiring anything in, look at what Provd sees for a wallet. This is the same check the [public scanner](/check) runs.

```bash
curl -s https://api.provd.tech/v1/counterparties/tron/TJ7E73Hs7aeeLDFMmySj9MGhXNronC6qc9
```

You get a score from 0 to 1000 (higher is riskier), a risk level, flags with reasons, and a summary of the wallet's recent USDT activity. This endpoint is rate-limited and uses public data only.

## 2. Score the trade before you release

When a buyer marks a mobile-money payment as sent and you're about to release USDT, send the trade as an intent:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.provd.tech/v1/actions/evaluate \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PROVD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order-48213" \
  -d '{
    "intent_id": "order-48213",
    "chain": "tron",
    "intent_type": "p2p_trade",
    "counterparty": {
      "wallet_address": "TJ7E73Hs7aeeLDFMmySj9MGhXNronC6qc9",
      "phone_hash": "9f2c6a1e4b7d3c8a0e5f1b2d6c4a8e3f7b9d0c2a4e6f8b1d3c5a7e9f0b2d4c6a"
    },
    "rails": { "fiat_rail": "mpesa", "crypto_asset": "USDT_TRC20" },
    "amounts": { "fiat": 65000, "fiat_currency": "KES", "crypto": 500 }
  }'
```

- `intent_id` is your own reference (an order id works). If you leave it out, Provd generates one.
- `Idempotency-Key` makes retries safe: the same key returns the same decision and is charged once.
- `phone_hash` is optional. Hash the phone number on your side (HMAC-SHA256 with your own secret, hex-encoded). Never send raw numbers; they are rejected.

## 3. Read the decision

```json
{
  "intent_id": "order-48213",
  "score": 1000,
  "risk_level": "critical",
  "risk_flags": [
    {
      "code": "CP_ADDRESS_FROZEN",
      "severity": "critical",
      "reason": "The counterparty wallet itself is on a public risk list (tether_usdt_freeze)."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "reject",
  "explainability": [
    {
      "signal": "counterparty_graph",
      "value": "address_flagged",
      "contribution": 1000,
      "reason": "The counterparty wallet itself is on a public risk list (tether_usdt_freeze).",
      "source_refs": ["tether_usdt_freeze"]
    }
  ],
  "signal_coverage": { "counterparty_graph": "full" },
  "decision_record_hash": "5b0f…",
  "engine_version": "2026.10.0",
  "latency_ms": 412,
  "created_at": "2026-10-03T13:11:16.891600Z"
}
```

Act on `recommended_action`:

| Score | Level | Action | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–249 | `low` | `release` | Release the funds. |
| 250–499 | `medium` | `manual_review` | Have someone confirm the fiat payment landed before releasing. |
| 500–749 | `high` | `hold` | Hold the funds and ask the counterparty for more. |
| 750–1000 | `critical` | `reject` | Don't release. |

Each entry in `explainability` says which signal moved the score and why. Show the `reason` strings to your ops team; they are written for people.

## 4. Report what happened

Your own history makes future checks sharper. When a trade completes, or when it's reversed or turns out to be fraud, tell Provd:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.provd.tech/v1/outcomes \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PROVD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "intent_id": "order-48213", "outcome": "reversed" }'
```

Outcomes: `completed`, `reversed`, `refunded`, `chargeback`, `fraud_confirmed`, `fake_confirmation`. You can also report against a `wallet_address` or `phone_hash` directly, without an `intent_id`.

The next time that wallet, phone hash or a wallet that traded with it comes back, your checks raise `OWN_REVERSAL_HISTORY`, `OWN_FRAUD_HISTORY` or `CP_PLATFORM_FLAGGED_EXPOSURE`. Your outcomes are used only for your own checks. They are never pooled with other platforms.

## Next

- [Pay as you go](/docs/pay-as-you-go): free quota, balance and top-ups.
- [Decision records](/docs/decisions): fetch and verify the record behind a decision.
- [API reference](/docs/api-reference): every endpoint, field and flag code.
